# frozen_string_literal: true

# Populates normalized_email for the existing users table incrementally.
#
# Design points for a production-scale backfill:
#   - Bounded batches (BATCH_SIZE) keep each update small; the table is
#     never loaded into Ruby memory because in_batches streams primary
#     key ranges and update_all pushes the transformation into SQL.
#   - The WHERE clause is the progress marker: only rows still missing
#     normalized_email are touched, so the run is idempotent, a partial
#     previous run resumes exactly where it stopped, and rerunning
#     after completion is a no-op.
#   - update_all sidesteps per-row callbacks and validations on purpose:
#     this is a bulk data repair, not a domain operation.
#   - The completion criterion is simply "no rows remain where
#     normalized_email IS NULL", which the WHERE clause makes directly
#     observable.
class BackfillNormalizedEmail
  BATCH_SIZE = 5_000

  def self.run
    User.unscoped.where(normalized_email: nil).in_batches(of: BATCH_SIZE) do |batch|
      batch.update_all("normalized_email = LOWER(TRIM(email))")
    end
  end
end
